newsitem.title: BELARUS: CIS summit postponed after Yeltsin's illness.
newsitem.headline: CIS summit postponed after Yeltsin's illness.

text.p: A Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit scheduled for Moscow on January 17, which Russian President Boris Yeltsin had been due to attend, has been postponed, CIS secretary Ivan Korotchenya said on Friday.

Korotchenya told Reuters after a meeting of the heads of CIS representative offices in the Belarussian capital that Yeltsin, in hospital with pneumonia, had requested the delay but that it was not linked to his illness.
The CIS secretary said more preparatory work had to be done before heads of states from the organisation, which groups 12 of the 15 former Soviet republics, could meet.
"We are proposing a delay to January 29, 30 or 31," he said. "I would not link the postponement to Yeltsin's cold."
Another reason was that not all heads of state were able to attend, in particular Uzbekistan's President Islam Karimov who had already planned another foreign trip, he said.
"It would be better not to hold this meeting in the absence of any of the heads of state, as Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) put it," Korotchenya said.
The summit, originally scheduled for December, had already been postponed once.
Yeltsin was admitted to hospital on Wednesday night, only two weeks after returning to work following a major heart operation on November 5.
Doctors treating the Russian leader said on Friday he was breathing more easily but there had been no dramatic improvement in his condition, the Kremlin said.
